subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: Show that the points in the Argand plane represented by the complex numbers −2 + 7i, −3/2 + (1/2)i, 4 − 3i, (7/2)(1 + i) are the vertices of a rhombus.

mark_split.label: Write the four points and the distance formula
Find the four sides and the two diagonals
State equal sides, unequal diagonals, and conclude

recall_prompt: Say how you would show that the four points make a rhombus — what you compute, and which two facts you compare at the end.
insider_note: A rhombus answer needs the two diagonals as well as the four sides: equal sides with unequal diagonals is what separates a rhombus from a square. The last mark is the sentence that states both and names the shape.

steps.label: Write the points
steps.margin_note: First mark. Expand (7/2)(1 + i) to 7/2 + (7/2)i before reading its point. Keep the fractions as halves — the arithmetic stays clean if every coordinate is written over 2.
steps.memory_tip: Expand (7/2)(1 + i) to 7/2 + (7/2)i before reading its point. Keep every coordinate written over 2.

recall.must_convey: That the four complex numbers are taken as the points A(−2, 7), B(−3/2, 1/2), C(4, −3), D(7/2, 7/2), and that the distance formula gives the lengths.
accept: write the four numbers as points, expanding seven by two times one plus i first
the points are minus two seven, minus three by two comma half, four minus three and seven by two comma seven by two
take real and imaginary parts as coordinates for all four
naalugu numbers ni points ga rayali, last di seven by two comma seven by two
convert each number to a point and use the distance formula

steps.why: A rhombus is four equal sides — a coordinate fact. The complex numbers are only used here, to give the four points; the fraction in D is the one place the reading can go wrong.
common_mistakes: Writing B as (−3/2, −1/2) — its imaginary part is +1/2.
Converting the halves to decimals and losing exactness inside the root.

steps.label: Sketch the rhombus
steps.margin_note: Worth no mark. The rhombus is tall and tilted; its diagonals AC (long) and BD (short) are dashed. Unequal diagonals is what makes it a rhombus and not a square.
steps.memory_tip: AC and BD are diagonals, not sides. Unequal diagonals is what makes this a rhombus and not a square.

recall.must_convey: That the four points are marked, joined in order A B C D, and both diagonals drawn. Naming the sketch is full credit.
accept: draw the four points and join them in order with both diagonals
sketch A B C D and draw the diagonals A C and B D
mark the points and draw the rhombus with its diagonals
naalugu points guruthu pettukoni rhombus geesi diagonals geeyali
plot the points, join them, then draw the two diagonals

steps.why: The sketch shows which four segments are sides and which two are diagonals, and it shows the diagonals are clearly different lengths — the picture matches the numbers that follow.
common_mistakes: Joining A to C as a side.
Drawing a square and then being surprised the diagonals differ.

elements.caption: Step 2 — the four sides AB, BC, CD, DA
Step 3 — the two diagonals AC and BD

steps.label: Find sides and diagonals
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Each side is √170/2 — the pairs 1/4 + 169/4 and 121/4 + 49/4 both add to 170/4. The diagonals are √136 and √34, which are not equal.
steps.memory_tip: Six distances, not four. Every side is √170/2; the diagonals √136 and √34 are different.

recall.must_convey: That the four sides AB, BC, CD, DA each come to √170/2, and the diagonals AC = √136 and BD = √34 are different.
accept: the four sides are each root one seventy by two and the diagonals are root one thirty six and root thirty four
compute six distances, all four sides are equal and the two diagonals are not
sides come to root one hundred seventy over two each, diagonals differ
naalugu sides root one seventy by two, diagonals veru veru vasthai
equal sides, unequal diagonals from the distance formula

steps.why: Four equal sides make a rhombus. The diagonals are computed to show the figure is not a square as well — a square is a rhombus with equal diagonals, and the question asks for the shape to be named precisely.
common_mistakes: A sign slip in (−2 + 3/2) or (−3 − 7/2), which both need the fraction subtracted from a negative.
Stopping after the sides — the diagonals are what separate rhombus from square.
Leaving BD as √136/2 and not noticing it equals √34, then comparing it wrongly with √136.

steps.label: Conclude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Say the sides are equal, say the diagonals are not, and name the shape.
steps.memory_tip: Two facts, then the name: sides equal, diagonals unequal, therefore rhombus.
lines: AB = BC = CD = DA = √170/2 — four equal sides.
AC = √136 ≠ BD = √34 — the diagonals are unequal.

lines.text: ∴ A, B, C, D form a rhombus.

recall.must_convey: That four equal sides with unequal diagonals make ABCD a rhombus and not a square.
accept: four equal sides and unequal diagonals so it is a rhombus
sides equal, diagonals not equal, therefore A B C D is a rhombus
since the sides match but the diagonals do not it is a rhombus not a square
sides equal kani diagonals equal kaadu kabatti rhombus
equal sides with different diagonals means rhombus

steps.why: The question is 'show that', so the shape must be named from the two facts. The unequal-diagonals line is what makes the word 'rhombus' the exact answer.
common_mistakes: Concluding 'square' from the four equal sides without checking the diagonals.
Ending on the last distance with no sentence.
